 Current Affairs 
 30 October 2026
 CCS Approves ₹40,000 Crore Next-Generation Corvettes for Indian Navy 
 Why in News? 
 The Cabinet Committee on Security (CCS), chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, has approved a project worth over ₹40,000 crore to build eight Next-Generation Corvettes for the Indian Navy.  
 The warships will be constructed by two public sector shipyards: Garden Reach Shipbuilders & Engineers (GRSE), Kolkata, and Goa Shipyard Limited (GSL), Goa. 
 The project aims to strengthen India's maritime security, improve naval combat capabilities and promote indigenous defence manufacturing. 
 Important Points  
 Number of Warship s: A total of eight Next-Generation Corvettes will be built for the Indian Navy. 
 Displacement: Each warship will have a displacement of approximately 2,000 tonnes. 
 Design: The vessels will feature an indigenous stealth design developed by the Indian Navy. 
 First Delivery: The first corvette is targeted for delivery by 2030. 
 Construction: All eight warships will be built in India. 
 Which Shipyards Will Build These Warships? 
 The project will be jointly undertaken by two major public sector shipbuilding companies: 
 1. Garden Reach Shipbuilders & Engineers (GRSE) 
 Headquarters: Kolkata, West Bengal. 
 It is a major public sector shipbuilding company under the Ministry of Defence. 
 2. Goa Shipyard Limited (GSL) 
 Location: Goa. 
 It is a public sector shipbuilding company under the Ministry of Defence. 
 The project will strengthen India's domestic shipbuilding industry and create opportunities for Indian defence manufacturers. 
 How Will Next-Generation Corvettes Strengthen India's Maritime Security? 
 Next-Generation Corvettes will be multi-role warships capable of performing different maritime security operations. Their induction will strengthen the Indian Navy's combat readiness and operational presence across the Indian Ocean Region (IOR). 
 These warships will help India : 
 Strengthen maritime surveillance and security. 
 Improve naval combat capabilities. 
 Protect important sea routes and maritime interests. 
 Enhance operational readiness in the Indian Ocean Region. 
 Respond more effectively to emerging maritime security challenges. 
 Significance of the Project 
 Strengthening Naval Capabilities: The new warships will improve the Indian Navy's ability to undertake multiple maritime operations. 
 Promoting Atmanirbhar Bharat: Indigenous design and domestic construction will reduce dependence on foreign defence suppliers. 
 Boosting Defence Manufacturing: The project will support Indian shipyards, defence industries and associated manufacturing sectors. 
 Enhancing Maritime Security: The warships will strengthen India's strategic presence across the Indian Ocean Region. 
 Link with India's SAGAR Vision 
 The project supports India's SAGAR vision, which stands for Security and Growth for All in the Region .  
 The vision aims to strengthen maritime cooperation, regional security and economic development across the Indian Ocean Region. 
 It also supports the Atmanirbhar Bharat initiative by promoting indigenous defence production and strengthening India's defence manufacturing ecosystem. 
 Conclusion 
 The approval of eight Next-Generation Corvettes marks an important step towards strengthening India's naval capabilities and maritime security. The project will also boost domestic shipbuilding, support defence industries and contribute to India's goal of becoming self-reliant in defence manufacturing. 
 Prelims Practice Question 
 Q. With reference to the Next-Generation Corvettes approved for the Indian Navy, consider the following statements: 
 The project involves the construction of eight Next-Generation Corvettes. 
 Garden Reach Shipbuilders & Engineers (GRSE) and Goa Shipyard Limited (GSL) will build these warships. 
 Each warship will have an approximate displacement of 2,000 tonnes. 
 The project is aimed at strengthening India's maritime security in the Indian Ocean Region. 
 Which of the statements given above are correct? 
 (a) 1 and 2 only
(b) 1, 2 and 3 only
(c) 2, 3 and 4 only
(d) 1, 2, 3 and 4 
 Mains Practice Question 
 Discuss the significance of indigenous warship construction in strengthening India's maritime security and achieving self-reliance in defence manufacturing. 
 FAQs 
 Q1. What is the Next-Generation Corvettes project? 
 It is a defence project to build eight advanced warships for the Indian Navy. 
 Q2. What is the total cost of the project? 
 The project is worth more than ₹40,000 crore. 
 Q3. Which shipyards will build these warships? 
 Garden Reach Shipbuilders & Engineers (GRSE), Kolkata, and Goa Shipyard Limited (GSL), Goa. 
 Q4. What will be the displacement and maximum speed of these corvettes? 
 Each corvette will have a displacement of approximately 2,000 tonnes and a maximum speed of around 30 knots. 
 Q5. What is the main objective of this project? 
 To strengthen India's naval capabilities, maritime security and operational presence in the Indian Ocean Region.
